clock_meridiem_am: Postposed morning daypart words that keep a bare 12-hour clock reading in
the AM half (meridiem offset 0), the am counterpart of
clock_meridiem_pm.voc.  "acht uur 's ochtends" == 08:00; only the noon edge
is rewritten (12 -> 0).  Bands: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale nl
-- ochtend/morning [06:00, 12:00) is the am half.  ("nachts" is NOT here:
the night daypart crosses midnight -- see clock_meridiem_night.voc.)
"om drie uur vanochtend" is 03:00 today even after it has passed.
clock_meridiem_night: The NIGHT daypart is a midnight-crossing BAND, not the morning/night AM
half it was previously grouped in: "drie uur 's nachts" (three at night) is
03:00 but "elf uur 's nachts" (eleven at night) is 23:00, and "twaalf uur
's nachts" is midnight 00:00.  Small hours 1..5 stay AM, late-night hours
6..11 are PM, twelve is midnight (the band-split lives in the resolver
_clock_hms).  The AM ceiling follows the CLDR nl nacht band [00:00, 06:00)
clock_meridiem_pm: Postposed daypart words that put a bare 12-hour clock reading into the
afternoon/evening half (meridiem offset +12), exactly as the de locale's
"nachmittags"/"abends" already do.  These are the Dutch genitive surfaces
that trail a clock reading after the fossilised "'s" particle
Bands: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale nl -- middag/afternoon
[12:00, 18:00) and avond/evening [18:00, 24:00) are the pm half.
"om acht uur vanavond" is 20:00 today without the clock's roll to tomorrow.
daypart_avond_nl: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale nl
Sources: Algemeen Nederlands Woordenboek, Instituut voor de Nederlandse
The avond runs to midnight; the nacht takes over after it.
daypart_middag_nl: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale nl
"vanmiddag" is the single-word today+middag surface, the sibling of
afternoon of the current day"; Wikiwoordenboek: "tijdens de middag van de
lopende dag".  The bare "middag" stays the noon landmark of
clock_landmark_720.voc, so only the fused word is listed here.
daypart_nacht_nl: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale nl
Sources: Algemeen Nederlands Woordenboek, Instituut voor de Nederlandse
"vannacht" is a single-word today/tonight+nacht surface, the ANW's own
entry and the Dutch shape of "vanavond"/"vanochtend" for this band.
daypart_ochtend_nl: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale nl
Sources: Algemeen Nederlands Woordenboek, Instituut voor de Nederlandse
"vanochtend" is a single-word today+ochtend surface, the Dutch shape of
English "tonight", and the ANW carries it as its own entry.
"vanmorgen" is a synonym of "vanochtend" the ANW also carries as its own
entry -- here "morgen" is the older word for the morning ITSELF (as in
"goedemorgen"), not the "morgen"=tomorrow relative-day word it is
everywhere else in this locale; the two never compete because "vanmorgen"
is a single fused token, not a split "van" + "morgen".

marker_at_counts: Clock prepositions that also introduce a counted group: a bare hour behind one
is doubtful only right before a word of marker_counted_noun.voc.  Attested in
the parity acceptance rows; no dictionary source checked, a native reviewer is to confirm.
marker_clock_lead: Words that open a clock time and belong to it. They fold only in front of
a number, a clock time, a clock fraction or a clock landmark.
Each word is shown opening a clock time on the page named in brackets,
om: Wiktionary "om": "at (a time): Ik sta om vijf uur buiten." [nl-om.wikitext.txt]; woorden.org "om": "op het tijdstip van vb: ik kom om acht uur" [woorden-om.txt]

marker_counted_noun: Nouns that count people or things a clock never takes: a bare hour behind a
clock preposition and directly before one of them is a count ("wave at 5
people").  Each word is quoted from its Wiktionary Noun entry
(https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/<word>); the fetched pages are kept with the audit.
man: Noun. "man, human male, either adult or age-irrespective"
marker_date_lead: Words that open a date or a clock time and belong to it.
Each word is shown opening a time or date phrase on the page named in brackets,
op: Wiktionary "op": "on; referencing a date: op maandag" [nl-op.wikitext.txt]
marker_dayparttoday: bare daypart surfaces lexically fused with TODAY: "vanavond"/"vanochtend"/
"vanmorgen"/"vanmiddag" already name today's own band, unlike the plain band words
"avond"/"ochtend" (which compose with the clock's own future-roll rule --
see test_nl_r117 in the en corpus for the documented convention).
marker_during: "in" is the locative preposition used with months ("in januari").
marker_holiday_indef: Dutch indefinite article that cannot precede a holiday name made of an
adjective and a weekday: "een goede vrijdag" is any good Friday.
marker_next: "aankomend [...] aanstaand": coming, next (Wiktionary nl, s.v. "aankomend", with the
example "Aanstaande woensdag komen mijn kinderen eten").
marker_ordlast: Dutch "last" ordinal determiner.  "de laatste zaterdag van augustus".
Attributive superlative of "laat" -> invariant "laatste".  Van Dale, "laatste".
marker_s: The fossilised Dutch genitive particle "'s" (from "des") that introduces a
postposed daypart ("'s avonds", "'s middags", "'s nachts", "'s ochtends").
The tokenizer strips the apostrophe, so the surface reaching the grammar is
a bare "s"; the clock orders consume it optionally before the meridiem word.

marker_until_amount: The interrogative that follows "tot" when the limit is an amount, not a time:
"tot hoeveel graden koelt het af?".  "hoeveel [...] vragend telwoord: welk
marker_upcoming: The words that name the first one that follows, never the one after it: "komende
avond" is this evening before it begins, "komend weekend" the coming weekend.
Each word is also in marker_next.voc, which moves a week, month or weekday forward.
